steps.message:
ModelGate is the static scanner our model registry runs on every uploaded artifact before accepting it. It lives in `/app/modelgate/` and the registry invokes it once per artifact as `python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output /tmp/report.json /path/to/artifact`, reading the JSON report described in `/app/docs/report-schema.md`. The red team has shown that artifacts which run code when loaded get past it, and that it also flags some legitimate models. Harden the scanner so that its verdict matches the registry policy in `/app/docs/threat-model.md` for every artifact that policy covers: an artifact is `malicious` when loading it with its format's standard loader, or invoking a function it exports, would execute attacker-controlled code, start a process, access files outside the artifact, or open a network connection, and `clean` otherwise. A missed malicious artifact and a flagged legitimate one are equally wrong.

The registry grades the scanner on its own held-out corpus, built to the threat model, not on the examples in `/app/samples/`. Those examples, their labels in `/app/samples/labels.json` and the harness `/app/evaluate.py` show the formats, containers and report format, but they do not cover every technique the threat model describes. Only `/app/modelgate/` is deployed, so everything the scanner needs must live there, and the command line and report schema above must keep working unchanged. Scanning must never cause any behaviour of an artifact to run: the registry runs the scanner in an isolated sandbox and treats any process it starts, any network connection it opens and any file it writes other than its report as a failed scan. The registry scans its held-out corpus of roughly 650 artifacts in one pass, invoking the scanner once per artifact; the whole pass must finish within 900 seconds and no single artifact may take more than 60 seconds, using only the Python packages already installed in this environment.

You have 28800 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.
I'll start by surveying the scanner, docs, samples, and evaluation harness to understand the current state before hardening anything.

results.content:
# ModelGate registry policy: what makes an uploaded model artifact malicious

This is the policy the registry grades scanner verdicts against. It is the
only definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it
but do not enumerate it.

## 1. Policy

An artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's
standard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of
the following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:

- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or
  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that
  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a
  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another
  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what
  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a
  finding.
- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.
- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the
  artifact itself.
- **(D) network**: open a network connection.

Every other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false
negative are equally wrong.

Capabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a
dictionary value `"subprocess"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant
tensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached
through a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a
`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the
first `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a
finding.

Standard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:

| Format | Loader |
|---|---|
| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |
| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |
| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |
| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |
| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |

## 2. Formats and containers in scope

| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |
| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |
| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | `torch.load` unpickles all five streams in order; the object pickle is the fourth |
| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |
| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |
| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |
| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |

Out of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,
TorchScript `code/*.py`, TFLite, PMML, XGBoost and LightGBM native formats,
Keras SavedModel `keras_metadata.pb`, HDF5 external links and virtual
datasets, archives with 64-bit sizes or zip64 extra fields.

## 3. Pickle semantics the policy follows

These are the facts of CPython's unpickler; the policy is defined in terms of
what the loader would actually do.

- `REDUCE` calls the callable with the arguments (a tuple: `pickle.load`'s C
  unpickler raises on anything else before calling); on a class that runs
  `__new__` and `__init__`. `INST` and `OBJ` with arguments construct fully.
  `BUILD` calls `__setstate__` on the object (for `functools.partial` that
  retargets the partial) or, when there is none, writes the state into the
  object's `__dict__`, which on a module rebinds its attributes for every
  later `GLOBAL`. These are the ways a capability executes. A dotted name in
  `GLOBAL`/`STACK_GLOBAL` (`Bdb.run`, `os.system` under module `shutil`)
  resolves attribute by attribute at protocol 4 and above and fails the load
  below that.
- `NEWOBJ` and `NEWOBJ_EX` call `__new__` only; argument-less `INST`/`OBJ`
  call `__new__` only when the target is a class, and call any other callable
  (a `functools.partial`, a function) with no arguments. `PERSID`/`BINPERSID`
  are resolved by the loader's own storage mechanism (`torch.load`) and
  execute nothing; plain `pickle.load` has no persistent-id handler and stops
  there. Importing a module executes no capability.
- A global that is only stored as data (placed in a container, bound as an
  attribute, memoised and never called) is not a finding, whatever its name.
  A global becomes a finding when the capability it carries is executed, no
  matter how it reached the executing opcode: directly, through the memo
  (`GET`, `BINGET`, `LONG_BINGET`), through `builtins.getattr`,
  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller`, `functools.partial`,
  `builtins.__import__` or `importlib.import_module`, or in a later stream of
  the same file. Those are examples, not a list: any route by which the
  loader ends up calling the capability counts, among them a module reached
  through `sys.modules`, `vars()` or another module's attribute
  (`shutil.os` is `os`), a name resolved by
  `pkgutil.resolve_name`, a function handed back by a wrapper such as
  `functools.lru_cache` or `copy.copy`, and a callable passed to something
  that calls it (`map`, `filter` or `itertools.starmap` once something
  consumes the iterator; `sorted`, `min` or `max` through `key`;
  `functools.reduce`; `operator.call`; a thread or executor started with
  it). A lazy iterator that is built and never consumed executes nothing.
- A nested loader reads what its own loader reads: `pickle.loads` and
  `pickle.load` read one pickle and ignore trailing bytes, `torch.load` on a
  legacy checkpoint unpickles all five streams, and embedded data that the
  pickle first decodes or assembles (`base64`, `zlib`, `bytes.fromhex`,
  concatenation, a `bytearray` literal) is judged after that step.
- Module aliases are the same module: `posix` and `nt` are `os`, `_pickle` is
  `pickle`, `_io` is `io`, and every Python 2 name the unpickler maps back
  with `fix_imports` (the `_compat_pickle` tables): `__builtin__` is
  `builtins`, `copy_reg` is `copyreg`, `commands` is `subprocess`, `urllib2`
  is `urllib.request`, `httplib` is `http.client`, and so on. Pickles written
  below protocol 3 carry those Python 2 names.

Representative capability-bearing callables (a seed list, not the policy;
anything with the same capability counts):

- (A) `builtins.eval`, `builtins.exec`, `builtins.compile`, `marshal.loads`
  with `types.FunctionType`,
  `runpy.run_path`, `runpy._run_code`, `timeit.timeit`,
  `code.InteractiveInterpreter.runsource`, `bdb.Bdb.run`, `pdb.run`,
  `numpy.testing._private.utils.runstring`, `logging.config.dictConfig`;
  nested loaders `pickle.loads`, `_pickle.loads`, `torch.load`,
  `torch.storage._load_from_bytes`, `numpy.load`,
  `numpy.lib.format.read_array`, `joblib.load`, `pandas.read_pickle`.
  `builtins.__import__`, `importlib.import_module`, `builtins.getattr`,
  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller` and `functools.partial`
  carry no capability of their own; they are the ways a capability-bearing
  callable is reached, and the call that reaches it is the finding.
- (B) `os.system`, `os.popen`, `os.execv`, `os.execvp`, `os.execve`,
  `os.spawnl`, `os.spawnv`, `os.posix_spawn`, `subprocess.Popen`,
  `subprocess.call`, `subprocess.run`, `subprocess.check_call`,
  `subprocess.check_output`, `pty.spawn`, `pydoc.pipepager`.
- (C) `builtins.open`, `io.open`, `os.remove`, `os.unlink`, `os.rename`,
  `os.replace`, `os.mkdir`, `os.makedirs`, `os.rmdir`, `shutil.copy`,
  `shutil.copyfile`, `shutil.move`, `shutil.rmtree`, `pathlib.Path.write_text`,
  `pathlib.Path.write_bytes`, `pathlib.Path.unlink`; a nested loader given a
  path instead of embedded data reads that path.
- (D) `socket.create_connection`, `socket.socket.connect`,
  `urllib.request.urlopen`, `http.client.HTTPConnection.connect` and
  `.request`, `ftplib.FTP.connect` and `ftplib.FTP(host)`,
  `smtplib.SMTP(host)`, `ssl.get_server_certificate`, `webbrowser.open`. The
  capability is in the call that connects: constructing a client object
  without a host (`socket.socket()`, `http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port)`,
  `ftplib.FTP()`, `xmlrpc.client.ServerProxy(uri)`) opens nothing.

## 4. TensorFlow op table (closed)

For TensorFlow graphs the table is the policy: an op listed here has the
capability listed, and an op not listed has none, wherever it appears.

| Capability | Ops |
|---|---|
| (A) code execution | `PyFunc` `PyFuncStateless` `EagerPyFunc` |
| (C) file access | `ReadFile` `WriteFile` `MatchingFiles` `MatchingFilesDataset` `ImmutableConst` `WholeFileReader` `WholeFileReaderV2` `TextLineReader` `TextLineReaderV2` `FixedLengthRecordReader` `FixedLengthRecordReaderV2` `TFRecordReader` `TFRecordReaderV2` `LMDBReader` `LMDBDataset` `ExperimentalLMDBDataset` `TextLineDataset` `TFRecordDataset` `FixedLengthRecordDataset` `DatasetToTFRecord` `ExperimentalDatasetToTFRecord` `SaveDataset` `SaveDatasetV2` `LoadDataset` `SnapshotDataset` `SnapshotDatasetV2` `LoadAndRemapMatrix` `GenerateVocabRemapping` `Save` `SaveSlices` `Restore` `RestoreSlice` |
| (D) network | `DataServiceDataset` `DataServiceDatasetV2` `DataServiceDatasetV3` `DataServiceDatasetV4` `RegisterDataset` `RegisterDatasetV2` `DistributedSave` |
| never a finding | `SaveV2` `RestoreV2` `MergeV2Checkpoints` `ShardedFilename` `ShardedFilespec` (the standard checkpoint saver that every real SavedModel carries), and every op not listed above |

Op names are exact and case-sensitive. Node names, device strings, attribute
values and tensor contents carry no capability.

## 5. Keras

A `Lambda` layer whose `function` carries serialized bytecode is (A):
`"function": {"class_name": "__lambda__", "config": {"code": "<base64>", "defaults": ..., "closure": ...}}`; so is a `Lambda` whose `output_shape` carries bytecode in the same form (Keras
calls it when it rebuilds the model), and so is any layer whose `activation`
is a `__lambda__` dict (in the generic form Keras writes for a lambda,
`{"class_name": "__lambda__", "config": {"value": ["<base64>", defaults, closure]}}`),
since Keras deserializes an activation through the same path. A `Lambda` whose function is a named function reference
(`{"module": "builtins", "class_name": "function", "config": "relu", ...}`),
a named activation, and every other layer type are clean. Layers are found wherever the JSON nests them: `layers`, the `layer` of
a wrapper, and the `config` of a nested model.

  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a
  finding.
- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.
- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the
  artifact itself.
- **(D) network**: open a network connection.

Every other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false
negative are equally wrong.

dictionary value `"subprocess"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant
tensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached

  `functools.reduce`; `operator.call`; a thread or executor started with
  it). A lazy iterator that is built and never consumed executes nothing.
- A nested loader reads what its own loader reads: `pickle.loads` and
  `pickle.load` read one pickle and ignore trailing bytes, `torch.load` on a
  legacy checkpoint unpickles all five streams, and embedded data that the
  pickle first decodes or assembles (`base64`, `zlib`, `bytes.fromhex`,
  concatenation, a `bytearray` literal) is judged after that step.
- Module aliases are the same module: `posix` and `nt` are `os`, `_pickle` is
  `pickle`, `_io` is `io`, and every Python 2 name the unpickler maps back
  with `fix_imports` (the `_compat_pickle` tables): `__builtin__` is
  `builtins`, `copy_reg` is `copyreg`, `commands` is `subprocess`, `urllib2`
  is `urllib.request`, `httplib` is `http.client`, and so on. Pickles written
  below protocol 3 carry those Python 2 names.

Representative capability-bearing callables (a seed list, not the policy;
anything with the same capability counts):

- (A) `builtins.eval`, `builtins.exec`, `builtins.compile`, `marshal.loads`
  with `types.FunctionType`,
  `runpy.run_path`, `runpy._run_code`, `timeit.timeit`,
  `code.InteractiveInterpreter.runsource`, `bdb.Bdb.run`, `pdb.run`,
  `numpy.testing._private.utils.runstring`, `logging.config.dictConfig`;
  nested loaders `pickle.loads`, `_pickle.loads`, `torch.load`,
  `torch.storage._load_from_bytes`, `numpy.load`,
  `numpy.lib.format.read_array`, `joblib.load`, `pandas.read_pickle`.
  `builtins.__import__`, `importlib.import_module`, `builtins.getattr`,
  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller` and `functools.partial`
  carry no capability of their own; they are the ways a capability-bearing
  callable is reached, and the call that reaches it is the finding.
- (B) `os.system`, `os.popen`, `os.execv`, `os.execvp`, `os.execve`,
  `os.spawnl`, `os.spawnv`, `os.posix_spawn`, `subprocess.Popen`,
  `subprocess.call`, `subprocess.run`, `subprocess.check_call`,
  `subprocess.check_output`, `pty.spawn`, `pydoc.pipepager`.
- (C) `builtins.open`, `io.open`, `os.remove`, `os.unlink`, `os.rename`,
  `os.replace`, `os.mkdir`, `os.makedirs`, `os.rmdir`, `shutil.copy`,
  `shutil.copyfile`, `shutil.move`, `shutil.rmtree`, `pathlib.Path.write_text`,
  `pathlib.Path.write_bytes`, `pathlib.Path.unlink`; a nested loader given a
  path instead of embedded data reads that path.
- (D) `socket.create_connection`, `socket.socket.connect`,
  `urllib.request.urlopen`, `http.client.HTTPConnection.connect` and
  `.request`, `ftplib.FTP.connect` and `ftplib.FTP(host)`,
  `smtplib.SMTP(host)`, `ssl.get_server_certificate`, `webbrowser.open`. The
  capability is in the call that connects: constructing a client object
  without a host (`socket.socket()`, `http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port)`,
  `ftplib.FTP()`, `xmlrpc.client.ServerProxy(uri)`) opens nothing.

## 4. TensorFlow op table (closed)

For TensorFlow graphs the table is the policy: an op listed here has the
capability listed, and an op not listed has none, wherever it appears.

| Capability | Ops |
|---|---|
| (A) code execution | `PyFunc` `PyFuncStateless` `EagerPyFunc` |
| (C) file access | `ReadFile` `WriteFile` `MatchingFiles` `MatchingFilesDataset` `ImmutableConst` `WholeFileReader` `WholeFileReaderV2` `TextLineReader` `TextLineReaderV2` `FixedLengthRecordReader` `FixedLengthRecordReaderV2` `TFRecordReader` `TFRecordReaderV2` `LMDBReader` `LMDBDataset` `ExperimentalLMDBDataset` `TextLineDataset` `TFRecordDataset` `FixedLengthRecordDataset` `DatasetToTFRecord` `ExperimentalDatasetToTFRecord` `SaveDataset` `SaveDatasetV2` `LoadDataset` `SnapshotDataset` `SnapshotDatasetV2` `LoadAndRemapMatrix` `GenerateVocabRemapping` `Save` `SaveSlices` `Restore` `RestoreSlice` |
| (D) network | `DataServiceDataset` `DataServiceDatasetV2` `DataServiceDatasetV3` `DataServiceDatasetV4` `RegisterDataset` `RegisterDatasetV2` `DistributedSave` |
| never a finding | `SaveV2` `RestoreV2` `MergeV2Checkpoints` `ShardedFilename` `ShardedFilespec` (the standard checkpoint saver that every real SavedModel carries), and every op not listed above |

Op names are exact and case-sensitive. Node names, device strings, attribute
values and tensor contents carry no capability.

## 5. Keras

A `Lambda` layer whose `function` carries serialized bytecode is (A):
`"function": {"class_name": "__lambda__", "config": {"code": "<base64>", "defaults": ..., "closure": ...}}`; so is a `Lambda` whose `output_shape` carries bytecode in the same form (Keras
calls it when it rebuilds the model), and so is any layer whose `activation`
is a `__lambda__` dict (in the generic form Keras writes for a lambda,
`{"class_name": "__lambda__", "config": {"value": ["<base64>", defaults, closure]}}`),
since Keras deserializes an activation through the same path. A `Lambda` whose function is a named function reference
(`{"module": "builtins", "class_name": "function", "config": "relu", ...}`),
a named activation, and every other layer type are clean. Layers are found wherever the JSON nests them: `layers`, the `layer` of
a wrapper, and the `config` of a nested model.

# ModelGate scanner contract

## Invocation

The registry runs the scanner once per uploaded artifact, from a working
directory that is not `/app`, with no environment variables beyond `PATH`,
`HOME` and `TMPDIR`:

```
python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path>
```

`<path>` is the artifact: a file, or a directory for a TensorFlow SavedModel.
The scanner must write exactly one JSON document to `<report.json>` and exit
with status 0 once it is written. Exit status 2 is reserved for a usage error
(missing or unknown arguments). Only `/app/modelgate/` is deployed to the
registry; the scanner may use nothing outside it except the Python packages
already installed in this environment. The registry's held-out corpus holds
roughly 650 artifacts and is scanned in one pass, one invocation per artifact:
the whole pass must finish within 900 seconds and no single artifact may take
more than 60 seconds.

## Report

```json
{
  "scanner": "modelgate",
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "<the path argument exactly as given>",
      "verdict": "malicious",
      "findings": [
        {
          "kind": "code-execution",
          "location": "archive/data.pkl",
          "detail": "REDUCE builtins.eval"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- `results` has exactly one entry per path argument, in argument order, and
  `path` repeats the argument byte for byte.
- `verdict` is `"malicious"` or `"clean"`.
- `findings` is a list that is non-empty if and only if the verdict is
  `"malicious"`.
- each finding is an object with exactly the three string keys `kind`,
  `location` and `detail`.
- `kind` is one of `"code-execution"`, `"process"`, `"file-access"`,
  `"network"`, `"unsupported"`.
- `location` names where the finding is (a container member, a pickle stream
  and opcode offset, a graph node, a layer path) and `detail` says what it is.
  Both are free text for humans.

An artifact the scanner cannot analyse must still receive a verdict. The
registry policy is fail-closed: report it `"malicious"` with one finding of
kind `"unsupported"` that says why.

A report that is missing, is not valid JSON, violates any rule above, or is
not written within the time limit counts as a wrong verdict for that artifact.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the ModelGate scanner over /app/samples the way the registry does and
compare its verdicts with /app/samples/labels.json.

Usage: python3 /app/evaluate.py [--samples DIR] [--scanner /app/modelgate/cli.py]

The scanner is invoked as a separate process per artifact, with the same
command line the registry uses, so this script never imports the scanner.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

KINDS = {"code-execution", "process", "file-access", "network", "unsupported"}


def run_scanner(cli, artifact, timeout=60):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        report = os.path.join(tmp, "report.json")
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-I", cli, "scan", "--output", report, artifact]
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None, "timeout", time.monotonic() - started
        seconds = time.monotonic() - started
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return None, f"exit {proc.returncode}: {proc.stderr.strip()[-200:]}", seconds
        try:
            with open(report, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                doc = json.load(f)
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            return None, f"unreadable report: {exc}", seconds
        return doc, None, seconds


def check_schema(doc, artifact):
    if not isinstance(doc, dict) or doc.get("scanner") != "modelgate":
        return "top-level object with scanner == modelgate expected"
    results = doc.get("results")
    if not isinstance(results, list) or len(results) != 1:
        return "results must hold exactly one entry"
    entry = results[0]
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"path", "verdict", "findings"}:
        return "entry must have exactly path, verdict, findings"
    if entry["path"] != artifact:
        return "path must repeat the argument exactly"
    if entry["verdict"] not in ("malicious", "clean"):
        return "verdict must be malicious or clean"
    findings = entry["findings"]
    if not isinstance(findings, list):
        return "findings must be a list"
    if (entry["verdict"] == "malicious") != (len(findings) > 0):
        return "findings must be non-empty iff verdict is malicious"
    for finding in findings:
        if not isinstance(finding, dict) or set(finding) != {"kind", "location", "detail"}:
            return "each finding needs exactly kind, location, detail"
        if not all(isinstance(finding[k], str) for k in ("kind", "location", "detail")):
            return "finding fields must be strings"
        if finding["kind"] not in KINDS:
            return f"unknown finding kind {finding['kind']!r}"
    return None


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--samples", default="/app/samples")
    parser.add_argument("--scanner", default="/app/modelgate/cli.py")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with open(os.path.join(args.samples, "labels.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        labels = json.load(f)

    rows = []
    for name in sorted(labels):
        expected = labels[name]
        artifact = os.path.join(args.samples, name)
        doc, error, seconds = run_scanner(args.scanner, artifact)
        if error is None:
            error = check_schema(doc, artifact)
        if error is None:
            entry = doc["results"][0]
            verdict = entry["verdict"]
            kinds = sorted({f["kind"] for f in entry["findings"]})
        else:
            verdict = "invalid"
            kinds = []
        rows.append((name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds))

    width = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)
    print(f"{'artifact':<{width}}  expected   reported   ok  seconds  findings")
    for name, expected, verdict, kinds, error, seconds in rows:
        ok = "yes" if verdict == expected else "NO"
        extra = ",".join(kinds) if error is None else f"ERROR: {error}"
        print(f"{name:<{width}}  {expected:<9}  {verdict:<9}  {ok:<3} {seconds:7.2f}  {extra}")

    malicious = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "malicious"]
    clean = [r for r in rows if r[1] == "clean"]
    caught = sum(1 for r in malicious if r[2] == "malicious")
    false_pos = sum(1 for r in clean if r[2] != "clean")
    invalid = sum(1 for r in rows if r[4] is not None)
    print()
    print(f"recall: {caught}/{len(malicious)} malicious artifacts reported malicious")
    print(f"false positives: {false_pos}/{len(clean)} clean artifacts not reported clean")
    print(f"invalid reports: {invalid}")
    print(f"slowest scan: {max(r[5] for r in rows):.2f} s")
    return 0 if caught == len(malicious) and false_pos == 0 and invalid == 0 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import io
import os
import zipfile

from modelgate import keras_scan, pickle_scan, savedmodel_scan
from modelgate.report import Result

PICKLE_EXTS = (".pkl", ".pickle", ".joblib")
TORCH_EXTS = (".pt", ".pth", ".ckpt", ".bin")  # .bin: a torch checkpoint or a plain pickle
H5_EXTS = (".h5", ".hdf5")


def scan_path(path: str) -> Result:
    name = os.path.basename(path.rstrip("/"))
    if os.path.isdir(path):
        return Result(path, savedmodel_scan.scan_saved_model_dir(path))
    ext = os.path.splitext(name)[1].lower()
    if ext in PICKLE_EXTS:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            return Result(path, pickle_scan.scan_pickle(fh.read(), name))
    if ext in TORCH_EXTS:
        return Result(path, _scan_torch(path, name))
    if ext in H5_EXTS:
        return Result(path, keras_scan.scan_h5(path, name))
    # .npy, .npz, .keras and compressed archives are not model formats the
    # scanner understands; nothing to report for them
    return Result(path, [])


def _scan_torch(path: str, name: str):
    """A torch checkpoint is a zip whose data.pkl holds the object graph."""
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        data = fh.read()
    if not zipfile.is_zipfile(io.BytesIO(data)):
        return pickle_scan.scan_pickle(data, name)  # legacy (pre-1.6) checkpoint: a pickle
    findings = []
    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as zf:
        for member in zf.namelist():
            if member.endswith("/data.pkl") or member == "data.pkl":
                findings.extend(pickle_scan.scan_pickle(zf.read(member), f"{name}!{member}"))
    return findings

"""Pickle stream scanning.

Walks the opcodes of a pickle with ``pickletools.genops`` and reports any
global reference on the blocklist.  ``GLOBAL`` carries the module and name in
its argument; ``STACK_GLOBAL`` (protocol 4 and later) takes them from the two
strings pushed just before it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pickletools

from modelgate.policy import PICKLE_BLOCKLIST, SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS
from modelgate.report import Finding

_STRING_OPS = {"SHORT_BINUNICODE", "BINUNICODE", "BINUNICODE8", "UNICODE", "STRING", "SHORT_BINSTRING", "BINSTRING"}
_MEMO_PUT_OPS = {"MEMOIZE", "BINPUT", "LONG_BINPUT", "PUT"}  # the pickler memoizes every string it writes


def scan_pickle(data: bytes, location: str) -> list[Finding]:
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    recent: list[str] = []  # the last two string pushes, for STACK_GLOBAL
    try:
        for op, arg, pos in pickletools.genops(data):
            if op.name in _STRING_OPS:
                recent = (recent + [str(arg)])[-2:]
                for needle in SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS:

"""Keras HDF5 scanning: Lambda layers in the model configuration."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

from modelgate.report import Finding


def scan_h5(path: str, location: str) -> list[Finding]:
    import h5py  # lazy: only needed for Keras files

    with h5py.File(path, "r") as fh:
        raw = fh.attrs.get("model_config")
    if raw is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(raw, bytes):
        raw = raw.decode("utf-8")
    config = json.loads(raw)
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for i, layer in enumerate(config.get("config", {}).get("layers", [])):
        if layer.get("class_name") == "Lambda":
            findings.append(Finding("code-execution", f"{location}:layers[{i}]", "Lambda layer"))
    return findings
"""TensorFlow SavedModel scanning: parse saved_model.pb and look for file ops."""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

from modelgate.policy import TF_FILE_OPS
from modelgate.report import Finding


def scan_saved_model_dir(path: str) -> list[Finding]:
    pb = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pb")
    if not os.path.isfile(pb):
        return []
    from modelgate.tfproto import saved_model_pb2  # lazy: protobuf is slow to import

    sm = saved_model_pb2.SavedModel()
    with open(pb, "rb") as fh:
        sm.ParseFromString(fh.read())
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    if not sm.meta_graphs:
        return findings
    graph = sm.meta_graphs[0].graph_def
    for node in graph.node:
        kind = TF_FILE_OPS.get(node.op)
        if kind:
            findings.append(Finding(kind, f"saved_model.pb:node[{node.name}]", f"op {node.op}"))
    return findings

import sys, pickletools, io, zipfile, gzip, bz2, lzma, tarfile, os, json
def dis(data, label):
    print(f"===== {label} ({len(data)} bytes) =====")
    try:
        pickletools.dis(data, io.StringIO()) if False else pickletools.dis(data)
    except Exception as e:
        print("  [dis error]", e)
def head(data,n=64):

with open(p,'rb') as f: data=f.read()

head(data)
magic = data[:4]
if magic[:2]==b'PK':
    print("-- ZIP members --")
    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as z:
        for n in z.namelist(): print("  ", n, z.getinfo(n).file_size)

Key observations: sample_17 is a false positive from the `SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS` bug (the literal `os.system('id')` is stored as dict data, and `operator.itemgetter(1)` is clean). Samples 06/08/09/22 look clean in their heads but are labeled differently, so the payload is likely later or in a concatenated stream. Let me dump tails and detect multiple streams.

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/work/streams.py <<'PYEOF'
import sys, pickletools, io
data=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read()
print("TOTAL", len(data), "bytes")
# Walk streams: genops yields until STOP; find offset after STOP by scanning
off=0
sidx=0
while off < len(data):
    sub=data[off:]
    last=None
    globals_found=[]
    reduces=0
    builds=0
    try:
        for op,arg,pos in pickletools.genops(sub):
            last=(op.name,pos)
            if op.name in ("GLOBAL","INST","OBJ"):
                globals_found.append((pos,op.name,arg))
            if op.name=="STACK_GLOBAL":
                globals_found.append((pos,op.name,"<stack>"))
            if op.name=="REDUCE": reduces+=1
            if op.name=="BUILD": builds+=1
            if op.name=="STOP":
                stop_pos=pos
                break
        else:
            print(f"stream {sidx}: no STOP (consumed {len(sub)} bytes from off {off})")
            break
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"stream {sidx} at off {off}: genops error {e}")
        break
    consumed = stop_pos+1
    print(f"stream {sidx}: off {off}..{off+consumed} (len {consumed}), reduces={reduces} builds={builds} globals={globals_found}")
    off += consumed
    sidx+=1
    if sidx>12: 
        print("...>12 streams, stopping"); break
print(f"trailing bytes after last stream: {len(data)-off}")

steps.message:
Now the structure is clear. Key lessons from the pickle samples:
- **sample_08** hides `posix system` (alias for `os.system`) in a **second concatenated stream** — the current scanner breaks at the first STOP.
- **sample_06** uses the `INST` opcode (`os system`), which the scanner doesn't check.
- **sample_18** (clean) calls `os.fspath` and **sample_17/22** (clean) are false positives from `SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS`.

Let me see sample_09's tail and confirm sample_22's bogus trigger, then inspect the non-pickle formats.

steps.message:
I now have a complete picture of all 30 samples and the techniques they use. Let me record the key findings to memory before the large implementation, then build the hardened scanner.

The plan:
- **pickle_scan.py**: replace the naive opcode-grep with a stack+memo abstract interpreter of the pickle VM that flags a capability only when it is actually *called* (REDUCE/INST/OBJ/BUILD/routed-call), handling aliases, memo, multiple streams, nested loaders, getattr/partial indirection.
- **policy.py**: precise capability tables (not names-as-data), alias maps, full TF op table, Keras `__lambda__` rule.
- **dispatch.py**: content-based detection, archive/gzip/tar/zip recursion (depth 3), npy/npz, torch legacy multi-stream.
- **savedmodel_scan.py**: all meta_graphs, graph nodes + library functions, pbtxt, closed op table.
- **keras_scan.py**: recursive `__lambda__` detection for both h5 and `.keras`.

- 05 .bin: urllib.request.urlopen -> network
- 06 pickle proto-0: INST opcode `os system` (not GLOBAL!) -> process
- 07 .joblib: os.system -> process
- 08 pickle: TWO concatenated streams; stream1 has `posix system` (alias os.system) -> process
- 09 pickle: STACK_GLOBAL pickle.loads + REDUCE on embedded bytes containing os.system (re-entrant/nested loader)

- 20 .h5: no Lambda -> clean

"""Minimal pickle opcode assembler for building test artifacts by hand."""
import struct

class P:
    def __init__(self, proto=4):
        self.b = bytearray()
        if proto >= 2:
            self.b += b'\x80' + bytes([proto])
        self.proto = proto
    def raw(self, x): self.b += x; return self
    def stop(self): self.b += b'.'; return bytes(self.b)
    def bytes(self): return bytes(self.b)
    # globals
    def glob(self, module, name):   # GLOBAL 'c'
        self.b += b'c' + module.encode() + b'\n' + name.encode() + b'\n'; return self
    def inst(self, module, name):   # INST 'i' (args already on stack after MARK)
        self.b += b'i' + module.encode() + b'\n' + name.encode() + b'\n'; return self
    def stackglobal(self, module, name):
        self.uni(module); self.uni(name); self.b += b'\x93'; return self
    def ext(self, code):
        self.b += b'\x82' + bytes([code]); return self
    # strings / bytes / scalars
    def uni(self, s):               # SHORT_BINUNICODE / BINUNICODE
        e = s.encode('utf-8')
        if len(e) < 256: self.b += b'\x8c' + bytes([len(e)]) + e
        else: self.b += b'X' + struct.pack('<I', len(e)) + e
        return self
    def uni_long(self, s):
        e = s.encode('utf-8'); self.b += b'X' + struct.pack('<I', len(e)) + e; return self
    def bin(self, data):            # SHORT_BINBYTES / BINBYTES
        if len(data) < 256: self.b += b'C' + bytes([len(data)]) + data
        else: self.b += b'B' + struct.pack('<I', len(data)) + data
        return self
    def int1(self, n): self.b += b'K' + bytes([n]); return self
    def none(self): self.b += b'N'; return self
    def true(self): self.b += b'\x88'; return self
    def false(self): self.b += b'\x89'; return self
    # containers
    def mark(self): self.b += b'('; return self
    def tuple0(self): self.b += b')'; return self
    def tuple1(self): self.b += b'\x85'; return self
    def tuple2(self): self.b += b'\x86'; return self
    def tuple3(self): self.b += b'\x87'; return self
    def tuplem(self): self.b += b't'; return self      # TUPLE (to mark)
    def emptylist(self): self.b += b']'; return self
    def append(self): self.b += b'a'; return self
    def appends(self): self.b += b'e'; return self
    def emptydict(self): self.b += b'}'; return self
    def setitem(self): self.b += b's'; return self
    def setitems(self): self.b += b'u'; return self
    def listm(self): self.b += b'l'; return self
    def dictm(self): self.b += b'd'; return self
    def objm(self): self.b += b'o'; return self        # OBJ (to mark)
    # ops
    def reduce(self): self.b += b'R'; return self
    def build(self): self.b += b'b'; return self
    def newobj(self): self.b += b'\x81'; return self
    def pop(self): self.b += b'0'; return self
    def popmark(self): self.b += b'1'; return self
    def dup(self): self.b += b'2'; return self
    # memo
    def memo(self): self.b += b'\x94'; return self      # MEMOIZE
    def put(self, i): self.b += b'q' + bytes([i]); return self
    def get(self, i): self.b += b'h' + bytes([i]); return self

def call(module, name, argbuilder, proto=4):
    """GLOBAL module.name ; args ; REDUCE ; STOP"""
    p = P(proto); p.glob(module, name); argbuilder(p); p.reduce(); return p.stop()
PYEOF

emit('p_compile.pkl', dumps(R(builtins.compile, ("x=1","<s>","exec")), 4), 'malicious')
emit('p_popen.pkl', dumps(R(_os.popen, ("id",)), 4), 'malicious')
emit('p_subpopen.pkl', dumps(R(subprocess.Popen, (["id"],)), 4), 'malicious')
emit('p_subcall.pkl', dumps(R(subprocess.call, ("id",)), 4), 'malicious')
emit('p_execv.pkl', dumps(R(_os.execv, ("/bin/sh",["sh"])), 4), 'malicious')

emit('p_rmtree.pkl', dumps(R(shutil.rmtree, ("/tmp/x",)), 4), 'malicious')
emit('p_urlopen.pkl', dumps(R(urllib.request.urlopen, ("http://x/",)), 4), 'malicious')
emit('p_createconn.pkl', dumps(R(socket.create_connection, (("h",80),)), 4), 'malicious')
emit('p_webbrowser.pkl', dumps(R(webbrowser.open, ("http://x",)), 4), 'malicious')
emit('p_getcert.pkl', dumps(R(ssl.get_server_certificate, (("h",443),)), 4), 'malicious')

emit('p_smtp_host.pkl', dumps(R(smtplib.SMTP, ("host",)), 4), 'malicious')
emit('p_ftp_nohost.pkl', dumps(R(ftplib.FTP, ()), 4), 'clean')
emit('p_smtp_nohost.pkl', dumps(R(smtplib.SMTP, ()), 4), 'clean')

p=P(4); p.glob('shutil','os.system'); p.uni('id'); p.tuple1(); p.reduce()
emit('p_shutil_os.pkl', p.stop(), 'malicious')

emit('p_memo_system.pkl', p.stop(), 'malicious')

emit('p_nested_zlib.pkl', p.stop(), 'malicious')

p=P(4); p.glob('pickle','loads'); p.bin(cleaninner); p.tuple1(); p.reduce()

p=P(4); p.glob('builtins','__import__'); p.uni('os'); p.tuple1(); p.reduce()

# PERSID (plain pickle has no handler; executes nothing) -> clean  (use BINPERSID)
p=P(2); p.emptylist(); p.put(0); p.mark(); p.uni('0'); p.raw(b'Q'); p.appends()  # Q=BINPERSID

p=P(4); p.glob('marshal','loads'); p.bin(b'\x00'*4); p.tuple1(); p.reduce()

# logging.config.dictConfig -> malicious
p=P(4); p.glob('logging.config','dictConfig'); p.emptydict(); p.tuple1(); p.reduce()
emit('p_dictconfig.pkl', p.stop(), 'malicious')

# py2 aliases below proto3: posix.system, __builtin__.eval, commands.getoutput
p=P(2); p.glob('posix','system'); p.uni('id'); p.tuple1(); p.reduce()
emit('p_posix.pkl', p.stop(), 'malicious')
p=P(2); p.glob('__builtin__','eval'); p.uni('1'); p.tuple1(); p.reduce()
emit('p_py2builtin.pkl', p.stop(), 'malicious')
p=P(2); p.glob('commands','getoutput'); p.uni('id'); p.tuple1(); p.reduce()
emit('p_commands.pkl', p.stop(), 'malicious')
p=P(2); p.glob('urllib2','urlopen'); p.uni('http://x'); p.tuple1(); p.reduce()
emit('p_urllib2.pkl', p.stop(), 'malicious')

# partial retargeted via BUILD: partial(os.fspath) then setstate to os.system, then call
p=P(4); p.glob('functools','partial'); p.glob('os','fspath'); p.tuple1(); p.reduce(); p.put(0)

import os, sys, json, io, zipfile, base64, shutil
import h5py
OUT='/tmp/work/kcorpus'
if os.path.isdir(OUT): shutil.rmtree(OUT)
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
labels={}
B64=base64.b64encode(b'\xde\xad\xbe\xef'*4).decode()
LAM_CODE={"class_name":"__lambda__","config":{"code":B64,"defaults":None,"closure":None}}
LAM_VALUE={"class_name":"__lambda__","config":{"value":[B64,None,None]}}
NAMED_FN={"module":"builtins","class_name":"function","config":"relu","registered_name":None}

def lam(function): return {"class_name":"Lambda","config":{"name":"l","function":function}}
def functional(layers): return {"class_name":"Functional","config":{"name":"m","layers":layers}}
def dense(act="relu"): return {"class_name":"Dense","config":{"name":"d","units":3,"activation":act}}
def minimal_h5_bytes():
    bio=io.BytesIO()
    with h5py.File(bio,'w') as f: f.create_dataset('x',data=[1,2,3])
    return bio.getvalue()

def emit_h5(name, config):
    path=os.path.join(OUT,name)
    with h5py.File(path,'w') as f:
        f.attrs['model_config']=json.dumps(config)
    labels[name]=label_for(name)

def emit_keras(name, config):
    path=os.path.join(OUT,name)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path,'w') as z:
        z.writestr('config.json', json.dumps(config))
        z.writestr('metadata.json', json.dumps({"keras_version":"3"}))
        z.writestr('model.weights.h5', minimal_h5_bytes())
    labels[name]=label_for(name)

LBL={}
def label_for(n): return LBL[n]
def H5(n,c,l): LBL[n]=l; emit_h5(n,c)
def KR(n,c,l): LBL[n]=l; emit_keras(n,c)

# malicious
H5('k_func_code.h5', functional([dense(),lam(LAM_CODE)]), 'malicious')
KR('k_func_code.keras', functional([dense(),lam(LAM_CODE)]), 'malicious')
H5('k_outshape.h5', functional([{"class_name":"Lambda","config":{"name":"l","function":NAMED_FN,"output_shape":LAM_CODE}}]), 'malicious')

H5('k_activation_code.h5', functional([{"class_name":"Dense","config":{"name":"d","units":3,"activation":LAM_CODE}}]), 'malicious')
H5('k_timedistributed.h5', functional([{"class_name":"TimeDistributed","config":{"name":"td","layer":lam(LAM_CODE)}}]), 'malicious')
H5('k_bidirectional.h5', functional([{"class_name":"Bidirectional","config":{"name":"bd","layer":lam(LAM_CODE)}}]), 'malicious')
H5('k_nested_model.h5', functional([{"class_name":"Sequential","config":{"name":"s","layers":[dense(),lam(LAM_CODE)]}}]), 'malicious')
KR('k_nested_model.keras', functional([{"class_name":"Sequential","config":{"name":"s","layers":[lam(LAM_CODE)]}}]), 'malicious')

# clean
H5('k_named_fn.h5', functional([dense(),lam(NAMED_FN)]), 'clean')
KR('k_named_fn.keras', functional([lam(NAMED_FN)]), 'clean')
H5('k_named_act.h5', functional([dense("relu"),dense("sigmoid")]), 'clean')
H5('k_no_lambda.h5', functional([dense(),dense()]), 'clean')
H5('k_decoy_name.h5', functional([{"class_name":"Dense","config":{"name":"__lambda__","units":3,"activation":"relu"}}]), 'clean')

"""TensorFlow SavedModel scanning.

Parses ``saved_model.pb`` (or ``saved_model.pbtxt``) and, for every meta graph,
inspects every op in the top-level graph and in every library function.  The
closed op table in the threat model (policy.TF_OPS) decides which ops carry a
capability; node names, device strings, attribute values and tensor contents
carry none, so only ``node.op`` is consulted.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

from modelgate import policy
from modelgate.report import Finding


def scan_saved_model_dir(path: str) -> list:
    pb = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pb")
    pbtxt = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pbtxt")
    from modelgate.tfproto import saved_model_pb2

    sm = saved_model_pb2.SavedModel()
    try:
        if os.path.isfile(pb):
            with open(pb, "rb") as fh:
                sm.ParseFromString(fh.read())
        elif os.path.isfile(pbtxt):
            from google.protobuf import text_format
            with open(pbtxt, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                text_format.Parse(fh.read(), sm)
        else:
            return [Finding("unsupported", path, "no saved_model.pb or .pbtxt")]
    except Exception as exc:
        return [Finding("unsupported", path, f"cannot parse SavedModel: {exc}")]

    findings = []
    seen = set()
    for mi, mg in enumerate(sm.meta_graphs):
        gd = mg.graph_def
        _scan_nodes(gd.node, f"meta_graphs[{mi}].graph_def", findings, seen)
        for fi, fn in enumerate(gd.library.function):
            fname = fn.signature.name or str(fi)
            _scan_nodes(fn.node_def,
                        f"meta_graphs[{mi}].library.function[{fname}]",
                        findings, seen)
    return findings


def _scan_nodes(nodes, where, findings, seen):
    for node in nodes:
        kind = policy.TF_OPS.get(node.op)
        if kind:
            key = (kind, node.op)
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            findings.append(Finding(kind, f"{where}.node[{node.name}]",
                                    f"TF op {node.op}"))

arguments.command:
cat > /logs/agent/sessions/projects/-app/memory/modelgate-scanner-design.md <<'EOF'
---
name: modelgate-scanner-design
description: Architecture of the hardened ModelGate static scanner in /app/modelgate
metadata:
  type: project
---

Hardened ModelGate scanner (`/app/modelgate/`), rebuilt so verdicts match `/app/docs/threat-model.md`. Invocation and report contract unchanged (`python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <r.json> <path>`). See [[modelgate-sample-techniques]].

Module map:
- `policy.py` — capability tables keyed by canonical `module.qualname` (CODE_EXEC/PROCESS/FILE_ACCESS/NETWORK → KIND_OF), HOST_SENSITIVE (connect-only-with-host), NESTED_LOADERS, router sets (GETATTR/PARTIAL/IMPORTERS/ATTRGETTER/METHODCALLER/CALLERS/REDUCER/MAPPERS/CONSUMERS/WRAPPERS/THREAD_STARTERS), MODULE_ALIASES + `normalize()` (uses `_compat_pickle` for py2 names; `_operator`/`_codecs`/`posix` etc.), TF_OPS (exact closed table, 42 ops).
- `pickle_scan.py` — abstract interpreter over `pickletools.genops` (never executes). Tracks stack+memo with abstract values (Const/TupleV/ListV/DictV/G/ModuleV/Partial/AttrGetter/MethodCaller/Lazy/Obj). Emits a finding only when a capability is CALLED (REDUCE/INST/OBJ/BUILD-retarget/routed). Resolves globals via safe introspection of allow-listed stdlib+numpy (canonicalizes re-exports like shutil.os.system, FunctionType→builtins.function). Handles: multi-stream (read to EOF, stop at first unparsable = legacy-torch raw tail), nested loaders (recurse payload via formats.scan_blob; path arg→file-access; BytesIO content), pure decoders (base64/hex/zlib/concat/join) to recover payloads, module-dict rebind via BUILD (module_overrides consulted in resolve_op), partial retarget. First stream unparsable → one `unsupported` finding.
- `formats.py` — content (magic) detection + archive recursion (gz multi-member/bz2/xz/zip/tar), depth cap 6, decomp cap 400MB. zip via `zipfile.is_zipfile`/EOCD (handles prefix bytes; last-dup-name wins via open(name)); keras-v3 (config.json) scanned as keras + members generically; npy object-dtype→pickle. Members >150MB with no container magic are SKIPPED (torch storages) not fail-closed. `top=True`→unsupported on unknown; nested/member→skip ([]).
- `savedmodel_scan.py` — all meta_graphs, graph_def.node + every library.function node_def, op→TF_OPS; pb and pbtxt.
- `keras_scan.py` — recursive walk of model JSON; flags any dict with class_name `__lambda__` (K3) or `function_type: lambda` (K2). h5 via path (lazy) or bytes; HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE set before import so no lock writes.
- dispatch: dir→savedmodel; file→peek 8 bytes, HDF5→scan_h5(path), else read→formats.scan_blob(top=True).

Verified: 30 provided samples + ~130 self-generated technique cases all correct (full recall, 0 FP, 0 invalid). Full 650-pass extrapolated ~70s (budget 900s), slowest single <0.6s. Writes only the report (no stray files, checked). Test generators in /tmp/work/gen_*.py (scratch, not deployed).
EOF

- `savedmodel_scan.py` — all meta_graphs, graph_def.node + every library.function node_def, op→TF_OPS; pb and pbtxt.
- `keras_scan.py` — recursive walk of model JSON; flags any dict with class_name `__lambda__` (K3) or `function_type: lambda` (K2). h5 via path (lazy) or bytes; HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE set before import so no lock writes.
- dispatch: dir→savedmodel; file→peek 8 bytes, HDF5→scan_h5(path), else read→formats.scan_blob(top=True).

steps.message:
The scanner is complete and thoroughly verified. The final run shows a representative result: sample_09's re-entrant deserialization is caught with a precise location (`sample_09.pickle@328»nested@64`, `REDUCE os.system`), proving the nested-loader payload actually gets scanned and the true capability reported.

## What was wrong

The baseline scanner matched on names and strings rather than capabilities. It scored 6/15 recall with 3 false positives because it:
- Flagged any data string containing `os.system`, `eval(`, or `subprocess` (false positives on clean models).
- Stopped at the first pickle `STOP`, missing concatenated streams; ignored `INST`/`OBJ` opcodes, memo indirection, module aliases, and nested loaders.
- Left `.npy`, `.npz`, `.keras`, and every compressed/archived format completely unscanned.
- Looked only at `meta_graphs[0]` top-level nodes for TensorFlow, missing library and conditional-branch functions, with a two-entry op table.
- Flagged every Keras `Lambda`, including clean named-function ones.

## What I built

I rewrote the analysis in `/app/modelgate/` to decide by capability, keeping the command line and report schema unchanged.

- **Pickle** is now an abstract interpreter over `pickletools` opcodes that tracks the stack and memo and flags a callable only when it would actually be *called*. It resolves aliases (`posix`→`os`, Python-2 names), reads all concatenated streams, recurses into nested loaders (decoding base64/hex/zlib/concatenation payloads), and follows `getattr`/`partial`/`attrgetter`/`operator.call`/`map`/module-rebind indirection, while treating a merely stored or imported name as clean.
- **Containers** are detected by content, not extension: gzip (multi-member), bz2, xz, zip (tolerating prefix bytes and honoring last-duplicate-name wins), tar, numpy `.npy`/`.npz`, torch zip and legacy checkpoints, nested to depth.
- **TensorFlow** scans every meta graph's nodes and every library function (including conditional branches) against the exact closed op table, in both `.pb` and `.pbtxt`.
- **Keras** flags serialized-lambda bytecode (`__lambda__` and `function_type: lambda`) wherever it nests, leaving named functions and activations clean.
- Anything unparseable fails closed as `unsupported`.

## Verification

Against the 30 provided samples: 15/15 recall, 0 false positives, 0 invalid reports. I also generated roughly 145 of my own artifacts exercising each threat-model technique the samples omit (every indirection path, host-sensitive vs no-host network, re-entrant deserialization, module rebind, all TF op classes with decoys, Keras nesting, archive edge cases, exotic opcodes). All pass with full recall and zero false positives.

A full-pass simulation projects about 70 seconds for 650 artifacts against the 900-second budget, with the slowest single scan under 0.6s. The scanner writes only its report (no stray files), disables HDF5 locking, exits 0 on success and 2 on usage errors, and imports nothing beyond the standard library plus the already-installed `h5py`, `protobuf`, and `numpy`.
